name: FlexInput Virtual Mouse
notes: Plain-HID virtual relative mouse (FunctionMode 0, no companion). 7-byte report: [buttons(5)+pad(3), X lo, X hi, Y lo, Y hi, wheel, hwheel] -- X/Y are int16 relative mickeys, wheel int8 (vertical), hwheel int8 (Consumer AC Pan, horizontal). No Report ID. Both wheels sit in a Logical collection with a Resolution Multiplier feature (logical 0..1 = physical 1..8, a 1-byte feature report: two 2-bit fields + 4 pad bits): mouhid SET_FEATUREs it to the maximum at start (the driver accepts every SET_FEATURE and forwards it to the output ring), after which one wheel count is 1/8 notch (WHEEL_DELTA 15) -- the smooth-scroll path. keymouse_hm reads that SET_FEATURE to learn the multiplier actually in force; its WHEEL_MULTIPLIER_MAX must match the physical max. x120 was tried (0xF1E4) and Windows did NOT apply it: each count scrolled a whole notch. Kernel-level pointer input via mouhid: immune to the user-mode injected-input filters that silently eat SendInput (ASUS Armoury Crate stack / hardened Win11 builds -- the reason this profile exists), and games see it as a real raw-input mouse. Reports are built directly by flexinput-virtual's keymouse_hm and published via HidMaestroDevice::write_raw_input; sub-pixel remainders carry across frames on the writer side. VID 0x1209 (pid.codes space, unregistered PID) -- cosmetic only for a ROOT-enumerated node; deliberately NOT 045E or gamepad-adjacent (see xbox360.json). PID bumped 0xF1E1->0xF1E2 when the report grew 6->7 bytes (added Consumer AC Pan / horizontal wheel) so Windows re-enumerates a fresh device and re-reads the new descriptor instead of serving a cached 6-byte one -- a stale descriptor on the persisted node was the suspected cause of dead mouse buttons after the change. Bumped again 0xF1E2->0xF1E3 for the Resolution Multiplier (x8), 0xF1E3->0xF1E4 for x120, and 0xF1E4->0xF1E5 back to x8 (same reason each time: the stale-node guard must destroy and recreate the persisted node).
